record.paper_title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
record.original_question: Let X1 and X2 be smooth projective varieties over a field, belonging to the same deformation class, and let Ku(X1) and Ku(X2) denote their Kuznetsov components, i.e. the geometrically meaningful residual admissible subcategories appearing after exceptional objects are removed from Db(X1) and Db(X2). Is X1 isomorphic to X2 if and only if Ku(X1) and Ku(X2) are equivalent as categories?

evidence.quote: Categorical Torelli problem. Let X_1 and X_2 be smooth projective varieties over a field

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k$ be a field. For a smooth projective variety $X$ over $k$, let $D^b(X)$ denote the bounded derived category of coherent sheaves on $X$. For certain deformation classes of smooth projective varieties (for example, Enriques surfaces, prime Fano threefolds, cubic fourfolds, etc.), $D^b(X)$ admits a semiorthogonal decomposition
$$D^b(X) = \langle \mathcal{K}u(X),\, E_1, \dots, E_n \rangle,$$
where $E_1, \dots, E_n$ is an exceptional collection and $\mathcal{K}u(X)$, called the Kuznetsov component of $X$, is the residual admissible subcategory which carries the geometrically meaningful homological information.

Categorical Torelli problem: Let $X_1$ and $X_2$ be smooth projective varieties over $k$ that belong to the same deformation class admitting a Kuznetsov component as above. Is it true that
$$X_1 \cong X_2 \quad \Longleftrightarrow \quad \mathcal{K}u(X_1) \simeq \mathcal{K}u(X_2)$$
as $k$-linear triangulated categories?
artifact.status_search_result: The categorical Torelli problem is a guiding conjecture that has been verified in several deformation classes (e.g. cubic threefolds without further assumptions, Enriques surfaces and cubic fourfolds under additional hypotheses on the equivalence, several prime Fano threefolds), but is known to fail in its naive form for Fano threefolds of index 1: there exist non-isomorphic birational Gushel–Mukai threefolds with equivalent Kuznetsov components. Hence the general statement is false as stated, while many refined or class-specific versions are open or solved case by case.

status_evidence.title: Categorical Torelli theorems: results and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews categorical Torelli theorems for Enriques surfaces, cubic threefolds, prime Fano threefolds, and cubic fourfolds, with various conditions on the equivalence.
status_evidence.claim: Many cases are settled (often under additional assumptions on the equivalence), while the general problem remains a research program.

status_evidence.title: IVHS via Kuznetsov components and categorical Torelli theorems for weighted hypersurfaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work establishes new categorical Torelli theorems for weighted hypersurfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Active progress is being made on additional classes.

status_evidence.title: New perspectives on categorical Torelli theorems for del Pezzo threefolds
status_evidence.snippet: Recent advances on categorical Torelli for del Pezzo threefolds.
status_evidence.claim: Several cases are now solved while others remain conditional.
